hook: "A couple (@brianshinsh) built a disposable camera app as a side project — 83 days later it earns them $20K/month"
idea: Once's best TikTok (10M views, 900K likes) is an AI UGC of a bride crying at her own wedding — the emotional moment carries a side-project app to $20K/mo in 83 days.
sequencing: Hook: couple's side project → $20K/mo in 83 days.
The best video: 10M views, 900K likes.
The content: AI bride crying at her wedding.
CTA: full breakdown thread.
Transcript: 'Oh.'
formatting: Side-project success snapshot: the build → the timeline → the money → the best video. Transcript: 'Oh.'
why_it_works: Crying is the strongest thumb-stop emotion — the viewer must know why she's crying. The side-project-to-revenue arc makes it feel replicable.
what_to_steal: The proof that a single emotional AI moment (crying bride) can carry an app to $20K/mo — LC's equivalent: an AI bride crying happy tears over jewelry that survived the wedding (sweat, tears, pool). Emotion-first, product as the quiet mechanism.

hook: "UGC videos with crying-face hooks can go viral."
cta: none explicit — the caveat is the content.
idea: Once's crying-bride hook drove 1M+ likes — but the creator has been 'getting married' for 6+ months, exposing the AI seams and raising the authenticity question.
sequencing: The mechanic: crying-face hooks go viral.
The example: Once's wedding-dress crying hook, 1M+ likes.
The tell: 'getting married' for 6+ months.
The verdict: basically no doubt it's AI.
Implicit: the authenticity caveat.
formatting: Analytical caveat post: the viral mechanic stated, the example, then the authenticity problem.
why_it_works: The detective framing ('getting married for 6 months') is satisfying media-literacy content — and it usefully pressure-tests AI UGC's weakest point.
what_to_steal: The authenticity guardrail for LC's AI emotional content: vary scenarios so no avatar is 'getting married for 6 months' — LC rotates AI brides across distinct stories. The 1M-like proof still validates the crying-hook mechanic.

hook: "Write am now and keep it till December then launch an ad to sell it as a digital product. 😂"
idea: A joke digital-product pitch — '2000+ Lessons 2026 taught me: 2000 lessons that broke me, made me cry and almost left me in shambles' — the emotional-lessons listicle as a product.
sequencing: The plan: write now, launch in December.
The title: 2000+ Lessons 2026 taught me.
The subtitle: broke me, made me cry, almost left me in shambles — and how I overcame.
The link.
formatting: Joke pitch: the plan ('write now, launch in December') + a full title/subtitle. One breathless paragraph.
why_it_works: The subtitle is a complete emotional arc (broke → cried → overcame) in one line — pain plus redemption is irresistible. The joke frame makes it shareable.
what_to_steal: The emotional-subtitle formula ('broke me, made me cry… and how I overcame') as LC's testimonial-story framing: 'what 3 years of green skin taught me (and the jewelry that fixed it).' Vulnerability-first titles earn the click.

hook: "this app pulled 22.5M views from just 2 AI UGC creators"
body: Once: 22.5M views from 2 AI UGC creators — an AI bride telling an emotional wedding story around disposable cameras ('we gave every guest a camera instead of hiring photographers'), Once as the product mechanism (QR → app). 13M top video, 9 over 100K.
idea: An AI bride's emotional disposable-camera wedding story with the app as the hidden mechanism — proof AI UGC moves product without looking like an ad.
sequencing: Hook: 22.5M views, 2 AI creators.
The format: AI bride's wedding story.
The mechanism: disposable cameras → QR → app.
The numbers: 13M top, 9 over 100K.
The proof: moves product without looking like an ad.
Research link.
formatting: Case study: numbers → format → proof line → research link.
why_it_works: The product hides inside the story's mechanism — viewers absorb the pitch while feeling the emotion. 22.5M from 2 creators proves story concentration beats volume.
what_to_steal: The hidden-mechanism structure: emotional story first, product as the plot device (not the pitch). LC's version: 'my wedding jewelry survived everything — here's the brand nobody told me about.'
